editorial_decision_gate.draft_heading: How to Prioritize Content Using Domain Authority and Organic Traffic Metrics
editorial_decision_gate.proposed_text:
To prioritize optimization tasks effectively, evaluate your content assets using domain authority metrics and existing organic traffic levels. Compile a list of your top-performing URLs from search console data and web analytics to establish a baseline performance list. Identify which high-traffic pages contain distinct factual assets but lack explicit source links in current AI summaries.

Divide your catalog into clear tier groups based on resource allocation needs. Assign high priority to core landing pages that combine strong organic traffic with high topical authority. Place secondary informational posts or low-volume assets into later optimization batches.

Execute targeted content updates on the highest-priority tier first. Add structured author details, explicit data citations, and clear summary blocks to those specific pages. Audit the updated URLs after publishing to monitor changes in citation frequency and source attribution.

additional_sections.heading: How to Run Manual Audits for Core Keywords and Conversational Queries
additional_sections.text:
Conduct a manual search for your top-performing target keywords and conversational queries across public generative engines. Open a fresh private browsing session to avoid personalized search history bias. Enter exact-match target terms along with common phrasing variations into the prompt box.

Document every source link and brand reference generated in the response text. Note whether competing websites appear in listed footnotes, and record instances where your specific page URLs are cited or omitted for key prompt variations.

Compare manual findings across multiple testing rounds to uncover consistent pattern gaps. Log these results in a tracking spreadsheet to determine which specific page sections require clearer formatting or direct factual statements.
